prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1136; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you were involved in at an intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state the location of the accident as best you can.

A: It was at a major intersection near a shopping center in Sugar Land. I was stopped at a red light in the right lane.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was waiting for the light to change. I had my foot on the brake and I was not moving at all.

Q: Describe what happened next.

A: The next thing I knew, I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped back and then forward. My car was pushed into the intersection a few feet.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: No, I didn't. I only saw it in my mirror a second before it hit me, and by then there was nothing I could do.

Q: Did you notice any injuries at the scene?

A: Right away my neck and right shoulder hurt. I told the officer about it. I didn't think much of it at first, but the shoulder pain got worse over the next day.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon and I have an appointment with an orthopedic doctor next week. I've been taking over-the-counter pain medication and I can't lift anything heavy with my right arm.

Q: Were you able to drive your vehicle from the scene?

A: No, the front bumper was damaged and the car wouldn't start properly, so it was towed.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I was not at fault. I was stopped and I did everything I could to avoid being hit.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
